decisions.reason: As a niche agricultural crate with only limited website presence and no sign of stronger follow-on promotion, it likely stayed below aspiration levels and does not justify continued resource commitment despite the firm's slack.
Its dedicated product page in both observed years suggests results at or above aspiration, and it fits the firm's core reusable-container business with strong cross-industry relevance.

Although only modestly promoted, a stackable plastic crate is close to the firm's standard portfolio, so with a large firm's slack and shared manufacturing base it is reasonable to retain it as a line-extending offering.

A medium-duty rackable pallet supports the core pallet range and likely benefits from existing production and sales channels, making it worth keeping unless performance is clearly far below aspiration.

The shift from a dedicated page to a mere mention points to performance falling short of aspiration, and this more specialized spill-retention item is easier to prune in favor of stronger core packaging products.

Despite reduced promotion after launch, the product remains closely tied to the firm's core pallet business and can be carried as a differentiated option while using existing capabilities and customer relationships.
